parts.note: Pop is a word for father and a festival is a special day, so the phrase is read as a music-loving celebration rather than the June holiday

explanation.surface: A question about whether a family holiday is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a reference to the annual holiday for dads, but it splits as 'Pop' (father) plus a festive day.
explanation.definitionFit: Read pun-wise, a 'pop' event lasting a day of celebration becomes a music gathering of bands and crowds.

definitions.meaning: to fancy is to imagine or envisage something in the mind
a film is also called a motion ..., a '...' for short

explanation.surface: Someone suggests going out to see a film.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine a scene is to see it in the mind's eye, and an old word for a cinema film is the same term.

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: set here means arranged or put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver who has parked says they can set the car alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges I CAN into ANIC, which follows P.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm in the sense of sudden fear is a synonym.

clue.text: You'll know when you've got it

definitions.text: You'll know when you've got it

parts.words: You'll know when you've got it
parts.note: read literally, once you possess this quality you know a great deal, since it means deep learning

explanation.surface: A reassuring remark that a feeling will be obvious when it arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Great scholarly learning means having knowledge, so having it means you know things.

clue.text: Drinks to the elevation of a good man

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevation lifts the letters upward, so the abbreviation is read bottom to top

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: Raising a glass in a toast to a worthy man's promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read a hidden run in 'Drinks to the' defined by 'good man', which cannot be a synonym of the answer; 'Drinks' is the definition, and 'elevation of' flips the saint upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Small measures of spirits such as whisky are called tots.

definitions.meaning: a pass performed by a matador, swinging the cape slowly past the charging bull

explanation.surface: A young woman put to death in a bullfighting arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' suggests killing, but here it means performed: the matador's cape pass has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a girl's name and a classic matador's cape manoeuvre in bullfighting.

clue.text: Grub is right at the centre of a burning issue

indicators.note: placed in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: molten rock issuing from a volcano is burning lava

explanation.surface: Food is said to be the key point of a heated debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning issue' looks like a hot topic but means what issues, burning, from a volcano; 'at the centre of' puts R inside LAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the young wormlike stage of an insect, the same thing.

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: building means constructing anew, so these letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A driver gathering pace notices traffic checks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges the word speed; 'checks' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning hinders.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hinder or obstruct its progress.

clue.text: Press cuttings-pins up the favourite ones

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pets are favoured people, like a teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone pins their best-loved newspaper clippings up on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PINS into SNIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Short extracts or scraps clipped from newspapers are small fragments of text.

definitions.meaning: the person who leads an orchestra in a musical performance
something that carries electric current, as a live wire does

explanation.surface: An energetic, lively person in the music world.
explanation.definitionFit: The person directing an orchestra shares a name with any material that carries electricity.

clue.text: Hastily make and hoist a flag

definitions.meaning: to sew a garment together quickly
to raise a flag up a pole

explanation.surface: Someone quickly sews and then raises a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a phrase for quickly stitching something together and for raising a banner up a mast.

clue.text: A ragged child may be an old city feature

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A poor child in rags is part of the historic townscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests a city landmark but is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is a poor, scruffy youngster.

clue.text: Such a player is presumably not equipped for the top

definitions.text: Such a player is presumably not equipped for the top

parts.words: Such a player is presumably not equipped for the top
parts.note: a sportsperson never chosen for the national side has won no caps; jokingly, they have no hat for their head

explanation.surface: A sportsperson thought not ready for top-level competition.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a 'cap' is awarded for playing for one's country, so a player without one has not been capped.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who has never represented their country has earned no international caps.

indicators.note: becomes signals a change of form, so the letters of the name turn into something new

explanation.surface: A woman named Dulcie takes up mathematics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' rearranges DULCIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek mathematician who wrote the Elements founded classical geometry.

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for 100, stands for many
oracles are sources of wise counsel

explanation.surface: A skill passed down by many sages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' seems to mean skill but is a boat. Coracles are small round boats, traditional in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a craft, and these are small round wicker boats.

definitions.meaning: openings in a ship's side that let water run away off the deck

explanation.surface: Elopements on board a vessel bring disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runaway affairs' suggests elopements; read it as things that let water run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck a plan is to sink it, and deck drains on a ship carry the same name.

clue.text: Sound of contentment about course from consumer

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a cat's purr signals contentment
a chase is a steeplechase course in horse racing

explanation.surface: A happy murmur coming from a shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the racing course inside the cat's sound; 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A consumer is someone who buys goods, a buyer.

clue.text: Titles count for a great deal here

definitions.text: Titles count for a great deal here

parts.words: Titles count for a great deal here
parts.note: suggests a place where noble rank matters, but means a shop where book titles are the stock

explanation.surface: A snobbish place where aristocratic rank matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling books depends on its range of titles.

clue.text: Switches on for one daily period

indicators.note: switches means swaps around, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Turning on a light for one part of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switches' looks like light switches but rearranges ON FOR ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning is a part of each day before noon.

clue.text: It comes from a conifer, naturally

definitions.text: It comes from a conifer, naturally

indicators.note: naturally hints at letters arranged in a free or wild way, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Something that grows on an evergreen tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naturally' rearranges CONIFER, and the whole clue also defines the seed case of such a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen trees produce woody seed-bearing cones.

clue.text: He could get his work done by Friday

definitions.text: He could get his work done by Friday

parts.words: He could get his work done by Friday
parts.note: sounds like meeting a weekly deadline, but refers to the castaway whose servant was called Friday

explanation.surface: An employee who can finish the job before the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Defoe's novel the shipwrecked hero's companion is named Man Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's castaway had a helper named Friday to do work for him.

indicators.note: form of means a reshaped version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school lesson on fractions in the top class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' suggests a school class but signals the anagram of HIGHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: These are parts obtained by dividing something into eight equal portions.

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock, so a pastry from there could be named after it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain bun can be bought in Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hard-crusted fruit bun has a rough surface like stone.

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length of twenty-two yards
a fetter or bond that restrains

explanation.surface: A gauge of how restricted something is.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a surveyor's length unit and also linked metal rings used to bind someone.

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: read as Gates-head, the head of the word gates, giving G

explanation.surface: A crowd breaks up in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' rearranges NORTH plus G. Gateshead is a town in north-east England, split here as the head of 'Gates'.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large crowd of people.

parts.note: astronomical suggests a huge number, but it means a figure in the stars: the hunter constellation

explanation.surface: A huge, sky-high number.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a well-known constellation of stars.

indicators.note: dual means doubled, so the piece is given twice

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, written as MI

explanation.surface: A woman driving on a dual carriageway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A female name, as of the heroine of La Boheme.

definitions.meaning: the Latin plural of opus, meaning works
staged dramas set to music and sung

explanation.surface: Something that functions and performs to a soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the plural of opus, and also sung stage drama.

parts.note: a penitent garment worn against the skin by those doing penance

explanation.surface: A pair of pitiful, worn-out pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' looks like pitiful but means penitent: the garment was worn as a penance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough cloth shirt worn next to the skin was a penance garment.

clue.text: They embrace the cloth before grace

definitions.text: They embrace the cloth before grace

parts.words: They embrace the cloth before grace
parts.note: suggests clergy hugging, but means table rings holding folded linen before the meal's blessing

explanation.surface: Clergymen hugging just before saying a prayer at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' usually means the clergy, but here it is a table linen square.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings hold rolled table linen until diners sit down.
